doc.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Rayburn Wright and her unorthodox methods
summary: Wright used her broken rules as class examples, and she valued his recognizing her own way of working.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Self motivated, and also because I didn’t have anybody really over my shoulder in those beginning stages where I was experimenting, I came up with my own unorthodox ways of doing things that I never dropped. And I remember Rayburn Wright in class, he used to pull out my things as an example and say, “Maria broke every rule I taught you last week here. But it works and this is why.” And so that was nice, I mean not always was it © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
good, but every once in a while he would say that, and I appreciated that he recognized that and allowed me to grow in those kind of unorthodox ways.
